name: Oli-Bidiman
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog lists only classification refs (Belew 2020, Ardener 1956, Guthrie 1953); no grammar/phonology located

sources.note: Lists Duala dialects after Maho (2009): Duala proper, Bodiman, Oli (Ewodi, Wuri), Pongo, Mongo; says Duala is a tonal language; nothing on stress. Phonology refs cited: Paulian 1971 (Esquisse phonologique du duala, Études bantoues I, SELAF, 53-88) and Helmlinger 1972 — both Duala proper.

sources.citation: Ebobissé, Carl. 1989. Dialectométrie lexicale des parlers sawabantu. Journal of West African Languages 19(2): 57-66.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. Lexicostatistic (dialectometric) comparison of 15 coastal varieties incl. 'l'oli' and 'le bidiman' (A.25 Oli in Guthrie; bidiman absent from Guthrie); result p. 62: subgroup '5. oli-bidiman' among seven subgroups; oli shares 58.3% with duala although geographically closest to it up the Wouri (p. 62). First-hand data on the variety, but no phonology.

sources.citation: Dinkelacker, Ernst. 1914. Wörterbuch der Duala-Sprache. Abhandlungen des Hamburgischen Kolonialinstituts 16. Hamburg: L. Friederichsen.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Duala-level (dual1243), not Oli-Bidiman. Vorwort p. V: words belonging to the neighbouring dialects 'Pongo, Mongo, Subu, Ewodi, Malimba u. a.' were excluded from the dictionary; Duala tones are set out (Hochton, Tiefton, Mittelton, plus Hochtief-, Tiefhoch-, Hochmittelton on one syllable). No mention of stress/Betonung/Akzent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent), nothing on Ewodi/Oli or Bodiman phonology.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page Oli-Bidiman (olib1234), with linked reference records 568881, 146227, 135249, 132874, 469495
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Only a classification comment: 'The language of Oli and Bidiman, a close relative of Duala is listed as a dialect of Duala [dua] in E16-E28. However, Oli-Bidiman is lexically (and otherwise) too distant from Duala to be intelligible (Carl Ebobissé 2014: 395, 409) to it, and thus merits an entry of its own.' Zero descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) references; the five refs are classification-only.

sources.citation: Ebobissé, Carl. 2025. Sawabantu: Vocabulaire comparatif de quinze parlers de la côte camerounaise (Bantu A.20 et A.30). BoD - Books on Demand. 211 pp. ISBN 9789956459926
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Recent French-language comparative 612-item wordlist of the 15 Sawabantu varieties including oli and bidiman, announced as one of two volumes; its introduction and transcription conventions may state the tonal/accentual system used for the oli and bidiman columns. Google Books shows a partial preview that our downloads could not reach.

sources.citation: Ebobissé, Carl. 2014 [©2015]. Sawabantu: Eine vergleichende Untersuchung der Küstensprachen Kameruns (Bantu A.20 und A.30). Schriften zur Afrikanistik 24. Frankfurt am Main: Peter Lang. 424 pp. (Habilitationsschrift)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: The only descriptive work with Oli-Bidiman data and a phonology chapter (Kapitel 2: Konsonanten, Gleitlaute, Vokale, Toneme, Bemerkungen per group; 2.6 Tonentsprechungen; 2.7 Silbenstrukturen); Glottolog's sole basis for the languoid (pp. 395-404, 409). Any tone/accent statement for Oli and Bidiman will be here, most likely in 2.2.4/2.2.5 (Zentralgruppe) and in 1.7 informant/corpus notes.

sources.citation: Ebobissé, Carl. 1976. Die Phoneme des Duala in ihrem Verhältnis zu Urbantu und Proto-Bantu. 126 pp. [Frankfurt am Main, thesis]

sources.citation: Ardener, Edwin W. 1956. Coastal Bantu of the Cameroons: the Kpe-Mboko, Duala-Limba and Tanga-Yasa groups. Ethnographic Survey of Africa, Western Africa 11. London: International African Institute (Routledge reprint 2017)
